Apply temperature, retain top-k logits if requested, then sort and retain the smallest nucleus whose cumulative probability reaches top-p. Keep the boundary-crossing token: dropping it can remove too much mass. Renormalize before sampling. Temperature zero uses argmax. A local generator makes tests repeatable without changing global RNG state; the function requires finite input logits.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** Temperature gives $p_i=\exp(z_i/T)/\sum_j\exp(z_j/T)$ for $T>0$. Nucleus sampling chooses a smallest sorted prefix whose probability mass reaches the threshold, then samples conditionally within it. Filtering changes the model's output distribution intentionally; it is not an exact acceleration of sampling from the original unrestricted softmax. [3](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/)
